$\blueD{20\%}$ $\greenD{\text{of}}$ $\maroonD{45}$ is the same as $\blueD{20\%}\greenD{\times}\maroonD{45}$.

To solve $\blueD{20\%}\greenD{\times}\maroonD{45}$, we need to convert $\blueD{20\%}$ to either a decimal or a fraction.

Percent means per hundred, so $\blueD{20\%}$ is equivalent to $\blueD{\dfrac{20}{100}}$ which is also equal to $\blueD{20\div 100=0.2}$.

 $\blueD{20\%= \dfrac{20}{100} = 0.2}$

$\begin{align}\blueD{20\%}\ \text{of}\ \maroonD{45}&=\blueD{\dfrac{20}{100}}\cdot\maroonD{45}\\\\
&=\blueD{0.2}\cdot\maroonD{45}\\\\
&=9
\end{align}$

Are any of the other choices equivalent?

The fractions $\dfrac{20}{100}$ and $\dfrac{1}{5}$ are equivalent. So:

$\blueD{\dfrac{20}{100}}\cdot\maroonD{45}=\blueD{\dfrac{1}{5}}\cdot\maroonD{45}$

The expression $\blueD{\dfrac{1}{5}}\cdot\maroonD{45}$ is equivalent to $20\%$ of $45$.

$\dfrac{20}{45}\cdot 100\approx 44.4$

The expression $\dfrac{20}{45}\cdot 100$ is **not** equivalent to $20\%$ of $45$.

$20\cdot 45=900$

The expression $20\cdot 45$ is **not** equivalent to $20\%$ of $45$.

The options that have the same value as $20\%$ of $45$ are:

- $\dfrac{20}{100}\cdot 45$
- $0.2\cdot 45$
- $\dfrac{1}{5}\cdot 45$
